acceptance.criterion_verbatim: Success-of-upstream is NOT the only trigger. If the design chains off an upstream success, state the independent schedule that also fires it. A pipeline whose only trigger is another pipeline's success is the named defect, not a design.
acceptance.invocation: aws events describe-rule --name cot-satellites-registry-producer-daily; plus a read of the applied .tf for any event-pattern or upstream-completion target
acceptance.output_evidence: ScheduleExpression cron(0 7 * * ? *), State ENABLED, EventBusName default; NO EventPattern field, and no success-of-upstream edge exists or is planned. The rule is a wall-clock schedule chained off NOTHING, so AC4 is satisfied BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by mitigation. The 07:00Z figure is DERIVED, not chosen: upstream cot-rebalancer-runner-daily is cron(0 6 * * ? *) UTC and lands at 06:00:43-44Z measured across 38 partitions, giving a 59-minute margin that stays CONSTANT because both clocks are UTC. That is also why an EventBridge RULE was chosen over this stack's aws_scheduler_schedule ET pattern -- the ET pattern exists for a MARKET-CLOSE anchor, and adopting it here would introduce the DST drift it was built to remove.
